domain: home-care visit logs reviewed by a care coordinator
role: Home-care coordinator reviewing each submitted carer visit log for a domiciliary care branch
setting: A domiciliary care branch where carers record each home visit on a mobile app. The coordinator reviews one visit log at a time against the client's care plan, recent visit history and the carer's notes. For each log they decide whether the visit was delivered as planned, whether it shows the client declining, what to do with the log and how urgently it needs attention. Logs vary widely: short visits, unsigned medication records, odd check-out times, changed observations and brief free-text notes. Alarming signals often come with benign explanations recorded elsewhere in the log.

delivered_in_full.instructions: The visit delivered the care plan in full for this slot.

criteria.true: Planned tasks done, time and attendance adequately met
criteria.false: Tasks, time, staffing or records fall short

client_decline.instructions: The log evidences a new decline in the client's condition.

criteria.true: Unexplained worsening shown against baseline or history
criteria.false: Stable, explained, or decline merely possible

next_step.instructions: What should the coordinator do with this visit log next?

criteria.accept_log: File the log as complete with no further action
criteria.hold_confirm: Keep the log open pending one specific confirmation
criteria.query_carer: Return the log to the carer to correct or explain gaps
criteria.escalate_clinical: Refer to the nurse or GP liaison for welfare review

consequence_if_wrong.instructions: How serious would the harm be if this decision were wrong?
criteria: Negligible effect, easily corrected later on
Minor inconvenience or a small avoidable cost
Noticeable harm, costly or slow to reverse
Severe or lasting harm to people or property

follow_up_urgency.instructions: How urgently does this visit need coordinator follow-up attention?
criteria: No follow-up needed beyond routine filing
Review within the week at routine check
Follow up before the client's next visit
Act today; client welfare may be at risk

factors.name: duration_shortfall_min
factors.description: Minutes the actual visit fell short of the planned duration; zero means on time or over.

factors.name: shortfall_explained
factors.description: Whether a short visit has a benign recorded reason, such as client asking to finish early or family taking over a task.

factors.name: task_completion
factors.description: Completion state of the planned tasks for the slot.

factors.name: medication_record
factors.description: State of the medication administration entry for the visit.

factors.name: attendance_anomaly
factors.description: Problems with electronic check-in and check-out records.

factors.name: anomaly_mitigated
factors.description: Whether an attendance anomaly has a benign explanation, e.g. approved alternative address, app outage logged, or manual time sheet countersigned.

factors.name: observation_change
factors.description: Size of change in recorded observations (fluid intake, food, skin, mobility, weight) against the care-plan baseline.

factors.name: change_explained
factors.description: Whether an observed change has a known cause already in hand, e.g. GP aware, planned medication change, recent hospital discharge plan.

factors.name: prior_concerns_30d
factors.description: Count of welfare concerns raised on this client in the last 30 days of visit history.

factors.name: carer_note_tone
factors.description: What the carer's free-text note conveys about the visit.

factors.name: double_up_status
factors.description: Whether the care plan requires two carers and whether the second carer was recorded.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether key values sit exactly on thresholds the policy leaves open, e.g. shortfall equal to the tolerance or one more prior concern than the review trigger.

factors.name: client_message
factors.description: Short message from the client or family attached to the visit.

sections.name: visit
sections.description: Visit ID, client ref, carer refs, planned and actual check-in/out times, location check.

sections.name: plan
sections.description: Care-plan extract: planned minutes, required tasks, carers_required, baselines, late tolerance.

sections.name: tasks
sections.description: List of tasks with status, and medication entry with signature and reason.

sections.name: observations
sections.description: This visit's fluid, food, skin, mobility and weight readings.

sections.name: notes
sections.description: Short free text: carer_note and optional client_msg.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Recent visits summary and dated concerns raised in the last 30 days.

rendering_notes: duration_shortfall_min shows only indirectly: visit.actual_in/actual_out timestamps versus plan.planned_min; never print the shortfall. shortfall_explained appears as tasks[].status 'client_declined' with a reason line, or a notes.carer_note sentence like 'Daughter arrived and took over lunch', or visit.early_finish_reason; absent otherwise. task_completion appears as tasks[] entries with status done/not_done/partial against plan.required_tasks; key_task_missed means a plan-required task (e.g. pressure-area check) is missing from the list entirely or marked not_done. medication_record: tasks.medication with signed true/false, outcome 'given'/'declined' and a reason string; section_null renders tasks.medication as null while plan lists meds_due true. attendance_anomaly: visit.actual_out null (missing_checkout), actual_out earlier than actual_in (checkout_before_checkin), or visit.loc_check 'outside_radius' (location_mismatch). anomaly_mitigated renders as visit.alt_address_approved true, visit.manual_timesheet 'countersigned', or history entry 'app outage logged' on that date; present about half the time when an anomaly exists. observation_change: observations values compared with plan.baselines (e.g. fluid_ml 600 vs baseline 1400, mobility 'hoist' vs baseline 'frame'); no field states 'decline'. change_explained: history entry such as 'GP reviewed diuretic dose 2024-05-02' or plan.notes 'post-discharge, expect reduced mobility'. prior_concerns_30d: count of history.concerns[] with dates in last 30 days. carer_note_tone drives notes.carer_note wording (one or two sentences): routine ('Settled, ate well'), ambiguous ('Seemed a bit quieter than usual'), explicit ('Found on floor by bed, says not hurt'). double_up_status: plan.carers_required 1 or 2 versus count of visit.carer_refs; required_absent may be mitigated by a note that family member assisted with hoist under agreed plan. boundary_case sets shortfall equal to plan.late_tolerance_min or prior concerns equal to the trigger count. client_message renders notes.client_msg (null when none). Decoys: carer names and refs, mileage_km, travel_min between visits, app_version, rounding of timestamps to the minute, 'thanks' messages on poor visits, complaints about carer punctuality on otherwise complete visits, observations slightly off baseline within normal variation. Records must never contain fields like 'status: incomplete', 'risk', 'urgency', 'decline: yes' or a recommended action; all answers must be inferred by comparing sections.
